```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Education is a state, local, and family responsibility, not a federal obligation, under the American constitutional system.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Over 90 percent of public school funding is state and local, not federal.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The role of the federal government in education must be progressively limited as control is returned to parents, teachers, and local school boards.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Programs such as \"Straight As\" legislation and \"Dollars to the Classroom\" are a good step towards returning power to the people.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Republican Congress rightly opposed attempts by the Department of Education to establish federal testing that would set the stage for a national curriculum.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Department of Education and each of its programs should be tested.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The federal government assumed a special financial responsibility to advance the education of disadvantaged children through the Title I program over thirty years ago.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"$120 billion has been spent on the Title I program.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The achievement gap between disadvantaged children and their peers has widened despite $120 billion spent on the Title I program.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The fiscal loss from the Title I program is not a good thing, but the human loss is tragic.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Another generation of children should not be written off.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Governor Bush's principles of local control, accountability, parental choice, and meaningful student achievement are endorsed as essential to education reform.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
